'''Fereydoon Abbasi-Davani'''{{Efn|{{langx|fa|فریدون عباسی دوانی}}}} (11 July 1958 – 13 June 2025) was an Iranian [[nuclear engineer]] and a member of [[IRGC]] who was head of the [[Atomic Energy Organization of Iran]] from 2011 to 2013.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Regalado |first1=Francesca |last2=Ward |first2=Euan |last3=Fassihi |first3=Farnaz |date=13 June 2025 |title=These Are the Top Iranian Generals and Scientists Killed by Israel |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/06/13/world/middleeast/iran-military-generals-killed-israel.html |access-date=15 June 2025 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=13 June 2025 |title=Iran's top military commanders, 6 nuclear scientists among 78 killed in Israeli strikes |url=https://arab.news/pytuh |access-date=15 June 2025 |website=Arab News |language=en}}</ref> A [[Iranian principlists|principlist]] who also served in the [[Islamic Consultative Assembly|Iranian Parliament]], he was killed in [[June 2025 Israeli strikes on Iran|an airstrike by Israel]] on 13 June 2025.<ref>{{cite tweet |last1=Fassahi |first1=Farnaz |user=farnazfassihi |url=https://twitter.com/farnazfassihi/status/1933341786665062811 |title=Breaking News: Iran's state television says deputy commander in chief of all Armed Forces Gen. Gholamali Rashid has been killed and nuclear scientist Fereydoun Abbasi.|number=1933341786665062811|access-date=13 June 2025 |date=13 June 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=David E.|last=Sanger|title=Much of Iran's Nuclear Program Remains After Israel's Strikes. At Least for Now.|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/06/13/us/politics/iran-nuclear-program-israel-strike-damage.html|website=[[The New York Times]]|date=13 June 2025|accessdate=13 June 2025}}</ref> He had previously been wounded in an assassination attempt in 2010.

== Early life and education ==
Abbasi was born in [[Abadan]], Iran on 11 July 1958.<ref name=aljaz1>{{cite web|url=http://english.aljazeera.net/news/middleeast/2010/11/201011297228879910.html|title=Iranian 'nuclear scientist' killed|agency=[[Al Jazeera]]|date=29 November 2010}}</ref> He held a PhD in [[nuclear physics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://kashmirobserver.net/2025/06/13/who-are-the-iranian-scientists-who-have-been-killed/|title=Who Are The Iranian Scientists Who Have Been Killed?|website=[[Kashmir Observer]]|date=13 June 2025|accessdate=13 June 2025|agency= Observer News Service}}</ref>

== Career ==
Abbasi was a professor of [[nuclear physics]] at [[Shahid Beheshti University]] and was reportedly a member of Iran's [[Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps]] (IRGC) since the [[1979 Islamic Revolution]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Survivor of Attack Leads Nuclear Effort in Iran|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2011/07/23/world/middleeast/23iran.html?pagewanted=all|access-date=17 August 2013|newspaper=[[The New York Times]]|date=23 July 2011|first1=David E.|last1=Sanger|first2=William J.|last2=Broad}}</ref> He reportedly performed nuclear research at the [[Atomic Energy Organization of Iran]] (AEOI). Prior to his appointment as head of the AEOI he chaired the physics department at [[Tehran]]'s [[Imam Hossein University]].<ref name=isis>{{cite web|title=Will Fereydoun Abbasi-Davani lead Iran to nuclear weapons?|first1=David|last1=Albright|first2=Paul|last2=Brannan|first3=Andrea|last3=Stricker|publisher=[[Institute for Science and International Security]]|date=24 June 2011|url=http://isis-online.org/isis-reports/detail/will-fereydoun-abbasi-davani-lead-iran-to-nuclear-weapons}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Galestan |first=Mansoureh |date=18 May 2021 |title=Iran's Election 2021: Who is Fereydoon Abbasi Davani? |url=https://www.ncr-iran.org/en/news/iran-election/irans-elections-2021-who-is-fereydoon-abbasi-davani/ |access-date=15 June 2025 |website=NCRI |language=en-US}}</ref>

Abbasi was appointed head of AEOI by then [[President of Iran|president]] [[Mahmoud Ahmadinejad]] on 13 February 2011 to succeed [[Ali Akbar Salehi]]. In his tenure, the AEOI was unwilling to cooperate with the [[International Atomic Energy Agency]] (IAEA). In fact, in May 2011, Abbasi was the recipient of a letter from the IAEA, where its Director General Yukiya Amano reiterated the agency's concerns about the "existence of a possible military dimension" to Iran's nuclear programme and stressed the importance of clarifying these issues, requesting prompt access to relevant locations, equipment, documentation and persons. In June 2011, Abbasi replied evasively, so much so that the IAEA Director could only repeat his request for credible assurances.<ref>{{cite web |first=Sasha |last=Henriques |date=6 June 2011 |title=June Board of Governors Meeting Convenes – Islamic Republic of Iran |website=IAEA |url=https://www.iaea.org/newscenter/news/june-board-governors-meeting-convenes |access-date=28 January 2018}}</ref>

Abbasi was removed from office on 16 August 2013 and subsequently replaced by Salehi.<ref>{{cite news|title=Iran Parliament approves big Rouhani cabinet nominees, rejects 3|url=http://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/Default.aspx?pageID=238&nid=52665|access-date=17 August 2013|newspaper=Hurriyet|date=16 August 2013|agency=[[Reuters]]}}</ref>

In 2020, Abbasi was elected to Iran's parliament (Majles), representing the city of Kazerun. His term began on 27 May 2020. In parliament, Abbasi continued to advocate for Iran's nuclear program and align himself with hardline political factions supportive of the country's defense and scientific development strategies.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kia |first=Shahriar |date=25 November 2024 |title=Iran News: Officials Call for Higher Enrichment, NPT Exit, and Even Nuclear Bomb Development |url=https://www.ncr-iran.org/en/news/nuclear/iran-news-officials-call-for-higher-enrichment-npt-exit-and-even-nuclear-bomb-development/ |access-date=13 June 2025 |website=NCRI |language=en-US}}</ref>

===Responsibilities and Executive Background===
*Deputy for Student Affairs and Culture, Shahid Beheshti University, 2007–2016
*Founder and Secretary of the Iranian Nuclear Association, 2006–2013
*Head of the Physics Department, Imam Hossein University, 2006–2014
*Head of the Research Institute, Malek Ashtar University, 2005–2010
*Deputy for Postgraduate Education, Imam Hossein University, 2007–2010
*Director of Departments and Advisor to the Student Affairs Office of the Ministry of Science, Research and Technology, 2007–2010
*Head of the Physics Education and Research Center, Imam Hossein University, 2007–2010
*Responsible for supporting the Jihad-e-Sazandegi War in Fars Province and participating in various operations from the beginning to the end of the Iran-Iraq War
*Head of the Atomic Energy Organization in the 10th government in 2010
*Vice President in 2010<ref>[https://farajnejad.ir/%D8%B2%D9%86%D8%AF%DA%AF%DB%8C%D9%86%D8%A7%D9%85%D9%87-%D9%81%D8%B1%DB%8C%D8%AF%D9%88%D9%86-%D8%B9%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%B3%DB%8C/ کاملترین زندگینامه فریدون عباسی | مهندس هسته‌ای و نظامی The most complete biography of Fereydoun Abbasi | Nuclear and military engineer]</ref>

==Iranian nuclear program==
Abbasi was regularly linked to the [[Nuclear Program of Iran]]. He had defended Iran's nuclear efforts as peaceful and essential to national sovereignty.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Avag |first=Robert |title=Will Fereydoun Abbasi-Davani lead Iran to nuclear weapons? (Rev. 1) {{!}} Institute for Science and International Security |url=https://isis-online.org/isis-reports/detail/will-fereydoun-abbasi-davani-lead-iran-to-nuclear-weapons/8 |access-date=15 June 2025 |website=isis-online.org |language=en}}</ref>

In a 2012 interview with ''[[Al-Hayat]]'', Abbasi acknowledged that Iran had intentionally misrepresented aspects of its nuclear program to the IAEA and Western intelligence agencies. He stated "Sometimes we show weaknesses where we are not weak. Sometimes we show strengths where we are not strong. Later this became evident in talks with the IAEA".<ref>{{Cite web |date=20 September 2012 |title=Iran's nuclear chief claims Tehran fooled UK's MI6 |url=https://www.jpost.com/iranian-threat/news/irans-nuclear-chief-claims-tehran-fooled-uks-mi6 |access-date=13 June 2025 |website=[[The Jerusalem Post]] |language=en}}</ref>

=== Designation by the UN ===
Abbasi was "listed in an annex to U.N. Security Council Resolution 1747 of 24 March 2007, as a person involved in Iran's nuclear or ballistic missile activities". This resolution imposes an asset freeze and travel notification requirements. Abbasi was described as a  "Senior Ministry of Defence and Armed Forces Logistics (MODAFL) scientist with links to the Institute of Applied Physics, working closely with Mahabadi" (also designated by the UN).<ref>{{cite web|date=24 March 2007|title=Security Council toughens sanctions against Iran, adds arms embargo, with Unanimous Adoption of Resolution 1747 (2007)|publisher=[[United Nations]]|url=https://www.un.org/press/en/2007/sc8980.doc.htm |access-date=28 January 2018}}</ref>

=== Sanctions ===
In December 2012, Fereydoon Abbasi was sanctioned by the [[U.S. Treasury]]. He was added to the [[Office of Foreign Assets Control]]'s (OFAC) Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List under the Non-Proliferation of Weapons of Mass Destruction (NPWMD) and Iran Financial Sanctions Regulations (IFSR) programs. This designation was issued under Executive Order 13382, which targets individuals involved in the development or spread of [[weapons of mass destruction]] and their delivery systems. As a result, any assets he may have had under U.S. jurisdiction were frozen, and U.S. persons were prohibited from conducting transactions with him.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Fereidoun Abbasi-Davani {{!}} Iran Watch |url=https://www.iranwatch.org/iranian-entities/fereidoun-abbasi-davani?utm_ |access-date=13 June 2025 |website=www.iranwatch.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Sanctions List Search |url=https://sanctionssearch.ofac.treas.gov/Details.aspx?id=15570& |access-date=13 June 2025 |website=sanctionssearch.ofac.treas.gov}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Non-proliferation Designations; Iranian Financial Sanctions Regulations Identifications |url=https://ofac.treasury.gov/recent-actions/20121213 |access-date=13 June 2025 |publisher=Office of Foreign Assets Control |language=en}}</ref>

In October 2023, the EU designated Abbasi-Davani under its Iran sanctions regime, imposing restrictions on his financial assets and freedom of movement.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Loading... |url=https://data.europa.eu/apps/eusanctionstracker/subjects/3780 |access-date=13 June 2025 |website=data.europa.eu}}</ref>

=== 2010 assassination attempt ===
On 29 November 2010, Abbasi was wounded and narrowly survived an assassination attempt on a [[Tehran]] street, as a man on a motorbike attached a bomb to his car as he drove to work.<ref>"[https://www.nytimes.com/2011/07/23/world/middleeast/23iran.html Survivor of Attack Leads Iran's Nuclear Acceleration]". ''The New York Times''.</ref><ref name=autogenerated1>[https://www.bbc.com/news/world-middle-east-11860928 Iranian nuclear scientist killed in motorbike attack - BBC News<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref> A similar bomb attack the same day killed another scientist, [[Majid Shahriari]], who also taught at [[Shahid Beheshti University]].<ref name=autogenerated1 /><ref>{{cite web|first=Catrina|last=Stewart|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/middle-east/bomb-blast-blamed-on-israel-and-us-kills-iran-nuclear-scientist-2146996.html|title=Bomb blast blamed on Israel and US kills Iran nuclear scientist|website=[[The Independent]]|date=30 November 2010}}</ref>

==Death==
Abbasi was killed on 13 June 2025 during the [[June 2025 Israeli strikes on Iran|June 2025 American-Israeli attack on Iranian scientists and military officials]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Live updates: Israel strikes Iran's nuclear and military sites |date=13 June 2025 |url=https://apnews.com/live/israel-iran-attack |access-date=13 June 2025 |work=[[Associated Press News]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Marsi |first=Federica |title=Israel kills nuclear scientists, strikes sites in Iran: Who did it target? |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/6/13/israel-kills-nuclear-scientists-strikes-sites-in-iran-who-did-it-target |access-date=15 June 2025 |website=Al Jazeera |language=en}}</ref> in [[Tehran]].<ref>[https://www.rokna.net/%D8%A8%D8%AE%D8%B4-%D8%A7%D8%AE%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%B1-%D8%B3%DB%8C%D8%A7%D8%B3%DB%8C-74/1130912-%D8%B4%D9%87%D8%A7%D8%AF%D8%AA-%D8%AF%DA%A9%D8%AA%D8%B1-%D9%81%D8%B1%DB%8C%D8%AF%D9%88%D9%86-%D8%B9%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%B3%DB%8C-%D8%AF%D8%B1-%D8%AD%D9%85%D9%84%D9%87-%D8%A7%D8%B3%D8%B1%D8%A7%D8%A6%DB%8C%D9%84-%D8%A8%D9%87-%D8%AA%D9%87%D8%B1%D8%A7%D9%86 شهادت دکتر فریدون عباسی در حمله اسرائیل به تهران]</ref>

=== Funeral ===
His funeral held on 28 June was set to take place along with those of all the top commanders killed during the [[Twelve-Day War]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-06-25 |title=Iran to hold funerals for top commanders, scientists killed in Israel strikes: State media |url=https://english.alarabiya.net/News/middle-east/2025/06/25/iran-to-hold-funerals-for-top-commanders-scientists-killed-in-israel-strikes-state-media |access-date=2025-06-25 |website=Al Arabiya English |language=en}}</ref>
